body.statement:
Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prof}}\), construct \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\)
and prove
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
 P\{\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
for every strength sequence.  On each critical component of
\(\mathfrak R\) whose value is evaluated by \(\mathcal V_\alpha\), prove
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|
 -L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), prove
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|
 \asymp L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n.
\]
The upper comparison must keep the local stochastic contribution
\(\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) separate from the remainders
\(\zeta_n\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont},n}\),
\(|\mathcal G_c|\exp[-C_{\mathrm{sep}}n\kappa_n^2h_n/4]\),
\(2\delta_n\), and twice the maximal probability of each fallback branch
in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\); the last four expected-length
remainders must be \(o(r_n)\), and \(\zeta_n=o(1)\).  No upper rate or
critical constant is claimed from \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\), from
population separation, or from marginal profiling alone.
body.justification: With the minimax lower frontier settled separately, the remaining task is a single total interval that converts finite-grid calibration into continuum-uniform honesty and a matching upper expected-length guarantee.
body.gap: Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) condition out a functional nuisance in Gaussian-process moment models, while Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024) invert weak-identification-robust tests at a known cutoff. None supplies the required certified four-cell continuum transfer, fallback control, or critical-face attainment under an unknown cutoff.
body.consumer: The interval would give a frequentist benchmark for unknown or administratively uncertain eligibility thresholds, including the binary HIV-retention application studied by Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas.

obligation.what_is_open: After relocating the proved all-strength lower comparison, uniform continuum honesty and minimax expected-length attainment for \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\), including the separately displayed upper-rate remainders and fallback probabilities, remain open.
obligation.obstruction: Exact-grid method-of-types calibration and population profile separation do not transfer a continuously indexed true cutoff and effect to the candidate-specific grids and inner--outer sieves. The frozen core still lacks uniform control of the moved-discontinuity strip, localized stochastic profile width, certificate and solver fallbacks, and the critical-face decision value; the unresolved critical experiment also prevents equality with \(L_n^\star\) on finite-positive faces.
obligation.attempted: The exact-grid feasible-truth event was combined with the established deterministic false-split gap, and the lower-risk part was attacked separately by the moving-cutoff coverage integral and the new fixed-cutoff bump continuum. This closes the entire minimax lower frontier but supplies no uniform continuum-transfer or profile upper-risk theorem.
obligation.partial_result:
The all-strength minimax lower comparison is now closed separately:
\(\text{thm:integrated-and-bump-lower-frontier}\) proves
\(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n\) for the entire declared
strength shell.  Its moving-cutoff component gives the stronger explicit
bound \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), and its fixed-cutoff
bump component gives
\(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge c_{\mathrm{fix}}
\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}\).  Independently, the established exact-grid
calibration proposition accepts a grid-aligned true pair with conditional
probability at least
\(1-\delta_n/(|\mathcal G_c||\mathcal G_\vartheta|)\), and returning
\(\Theta\) on every listed fallback preserves that coverage.  The
established population separation theorem supplies the deterministic gap
\(C_{\mathrm{sep}}\kappa_n^2\min\{|c-c_P|,h_n\}\).  These are the complete
lower, exact-grid calibration, and population-localization layers; they
do not prove continuum honesty or the profile interval's upper risk.
